sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Smith Machine Push Up is a pressing exercise that uses a fixed barbell on a Smith machine to perform an inclined push-up.

By adjusting the bar height, the difficulty of the movement can be precisely scaled, making it accessible for beginners and useful as a finisher for advanced lifters.

The exercise primarily targets the chest with strong secondary involvement of the triceps and anterior shoulders.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Targets the chest, triceps, and anterior shoulders
- Adjustable bar height allows precise difficulty scaling
- Stable bar path supports learning proper push-up mechanics
- Wrist-friendly compared to floor push-ups for some lifters
- Reinforces core and full-body bracing
- Useful as a regression or progression for bodyweight push-ups
- Easy to load by lowering the bar to increase resistance

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Pectoralis Major

Secondary: Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids, Core, Serratus Anterior

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Set the bar on a Smith machine to a low to mid height that allows comfortable push-ups.
2. Confirm the safety stops are engaged and the bar is locked at the chosen height.
3. Position yourself facing the bar, ready to take a plank position underneath it.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Lie face down under the bar with hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Press up so your arms are fully extended and your body is in a straight line.
3. Brace the core and squeeze the glutes to maintain a flat plank.

sections.heading: Lower
sections.content:
1. Bend the elbows to lower your body toward the bar.
2. Lower until your chest nearly touches the bar.
3. Keep your body straight and your core engaged throughout the descent.

sections.heading: Press and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Press up through your hands by extending the elbows.
2. Drive evenly through both palms.
3. Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Letting the hips sag or pike up
- Flaring the elbows out wide
- Failing to lower through a full range of motion
- Choosing a bar height that is too low for current strength
- Letting the head drop or jut forward
- Holding the breath through the rep
- Rocking the torso instead of pressing through both hands evenly

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Smith machine with adjustable bar height
- Athletic shoes for foot traction
- Optional: Mat for forearm or knee comfort
- Optional: Mirror to monitor form

sections.heading: Bar Adjustments
sections.content:
1. Set the bar at a height that allows you to maintain good form for the desired reps.
2. Lower the bar for a harder variation; raise it for an easier variation.
3. Engage the safety stops to lock the bar in place.
4. Confirm the bar is stable before getting under it.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet hip-width apart, toes on the floor.
2. Torso: Straight line from head to heels, glutes and core engaged.
3. Arms: Hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, elbows tracking back at about 45 degrees.
4. Shoulders: Packed and away from the ears.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes slightly forward of the hands.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Bodyweight Push Up: Standard floor variation
- Incline Push Up: Hands elevated on a bench or box
- Decline Push Up: Feet elevated for greater chest demand
- Close Grip Push Up: Triceps-focused bodyweight variation
- Bench Press: Loaded barbell pressing
- Dumbbell Bench Press: Dumbbell pressing variation

sections.heading: Smith Machine Push Up Variations
sections.content:
Standard Smith Machine Push Up: Described here
Close Grip Smith Machine Push Up: Hands narrower for triceps emphasis
Wide Grip Smith Machine Push Up: Hands wider for chest emphasis
Feet-Elevated Smith Machine Push Up: Feet on a bench for greater load
Tempo Smith Machine Push Up: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy
Pause Smith Machine Push Up: Pause near the bar for greater chest tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Wrist Pain: Use push-up handles or grip the bar with neutral wrists
Elbow Pain: Reduce range of motion and lighten the demand by raising the bar
Shoulder Issues: Keep the elbows tucked at about 45 degrees
Low Strength: Raise the bar height for an easier angle
Advanced: Lower the bar height or elevate the feet
Beginners: Start with the bar high and progress lower over time
